newsitem.title: UK: UK calls for the West to open markets to the East.
newsitem.headline: UK calls for the West to open markets to the East.

text.p: Britain on Monday called for the European Union to open its markets to Eastern Europe and Central Asian exports to help those countries create stable market economies.

Speaking at a conference on trade and economic transition in eastern Europe and Central Asia, Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said the European Union had been "less than generous" both to the applicants for membership and to eastern exports.
"...the most valuable assistance we can give in the transformation of Eastern Europe and Central Asia into market economies is to open our own markets to their exports," he said.

Insisting that it was in the EU's own interest to allow easier access to EU markets, Rifkind accused the EU of harbouring protectionist sentiment. Free trade, he said, would help consumers by driving down prices -- and exporters through expanded opportunities for trade.
"Not everyone in the world has yet accepted the logic of free market," he said.
"In some areas, particularly in agriculture, the EU still is still forcing its consumers to pay for rates of subsidy to producers which would make a Soviet central planner blush."
